newsitem.title: GERMANY: Linde expects higher 97 sales, profit.
newsitem.headline: Linde expects higher 97 sales, profit.

text.p: German plant and engineering group Linde AG said on Tuesday it expected to improve its earnings and sales in 1997 after sales rose 6.4 percent in the first four months of the year.

Outgoing chief executive Hans Meinhardt said in a speech prepared for delivery at a news conference that growth would continue to come from foreign business and the company wanted a stronger position in Europe, South East Asia and the U.S.
The share of foreign business in overall sales would continue to grow, he said.
The company would continue to prioritise improving its products, cutting costs and further strengthening its earnings power.
In 1996, Linde's sales were 8.8 billion marks and earnings from ordinary activities were 689 million marks.
The company reported four month sales of 2.749 billion marks and said its incoming orders in the period rose 12 percent to 3.143 billion marks.
Future growth would come from within the Linde group and through acquisitions, Meinhardt said.
Linde is aiming to raise its sales in the medium term to 14 billion marks, based on its current four business areas -- plant construction, hydraulics, refrigeration technology and technical gases.
Meinhardt repeated that the company also aimed to add a fifth core business area.
